newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia CCM plant to start in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia CCM plant to start in 1999.

text.p: Chemical Company of Malaysia Bhd (CCM) expects its new chlor-alkali plant to commence operations by 1999, the national Bernama news agency reported on Tuesday.
CCM chairman Sheriff Mohamed was quoted as saying that a detailed feasibility study on the project would be conducted within the next few months.
The plant, which will make the basic chemicals used in the manufacture of poly vinyl chloride (PVC) plastics, is expected to cost approximately one billion ringgit.
It is a joint venture between Malaysia's state oil and gas company Petronas and a Japanese consortium.
Located in the northern Malaysian state of Terengganu, it is expected to be able to produce around 240,000 tonnes of chlor-alkali chemicals, used in the plastics industry.
Sheriff said CCM was also planning to build a 10-15 million ringgit plant to manufacture coagulant chemicals used in water treatment.
